name: Coda
verdict: No developer OAuth app was confirmed: each customer generates an API token in their account settings and pastes it in, about 1-3 days. Whether OAuth or MCP exists is unconfirmed.
needGuide: No — just collect each customer's API token (My account → API settings, path unconfirmed).

auth.detail: The Coda API v1 uses a per-user bearer API token (UUID format, shown once, from My account). An unrestricted token can do anything its owner can; restricted tokens (by read/write and by doc or table) are described as under development on the docs page. No OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow for third-party apps was found in the docs reviewed. Packs OAuth works the other way (Coda to third-party services).

effort.timeToProduction: 1-3 days (token paste UX); OAuth route unknown

approval.gate: None for token use. There is no developer-registered OAuth app to approve. If an OAuth or MCP option exists it was not confirmed.

scopes.why: No OAuth scopes; tokens follow the owner's access, optionally narrowed per doc or operation.
scopes.summary: No OAuth scopes. Token permission follows the owner's access, optionally narrowed by operation (read/write) or object (single doc/table) if restricted tokens are available.

cost: Free; API usage depends on the token owner's workspace role
prerequisites: Account and owner: Any Coda user can create a token for testing; use a dedicated service-account user for your own test docs.
Where you register: Each user creates their own token in Coda → My account (account settings) → API settings → Generate API token; there is no developer-registered app
Cost: Free; API usage depends on the token owner's workspace role

registerAt.path: Each user creates their own token in Coda → My account (account settings) → API settings → Generate API token; there is no developer-registered app

steps.do: Show customers where to create a token: Coda → My account → API settings → Generate API token, and what access you need
Offer a secure paste field; store the token encrypted, never log it, and mask it in the UI
Validate immediately with GET /whoami and a test doc list call; show the connected user name
Recommend that customers create a dedicated agent user and share only the needed docs with it, then use that user's token
Add a disconnect button that deletes the stored token and tells the user to delete it in Coda
Ask Coda support or check current docs about OAuth or restricted-token availability before launch

roles.team: Any Coda user can create a token for testing; use a dedicated service-account user for your own test docs.
roles.console: none documented (no developer console for the REST API).
roles.customer: Each customer user generates and pastes their own token; it works with their workspace role (e.g. creating docs needs Doc Maker or Admin). Workspace admin controls on API tokens not confirmed.

testing: Create a free Coda account, generate a token, and call GET /whoami.
Use a restricted token if available.

blockers.problem: Tokens are user-level and shown once
blockers.fix: Instruct users to copy immediately and keep a key rotation path.

blockers.problem: Unrestricted tokens grant everything the user can do
blockers.fix: Prefer a dedicated agent user or restricted tokens.

blockers.problem: Role limits can fail calls (e.g. createDoc needs Doc Maker or Admin)
Pasted tokens are weak for enterprise security reviews
blockers.fix: Be ready to explain storage and offer MCP/OAuth if Coda adds it.

automation.agentCan: Write the token-paste UX, secure storage, validation calls, and customer instructions, and run test API calls.
automation.humanMust: Each customer user creates their token in Coda; the developer confirms any OAuth or partnership options with Coda.

uncertain: Whether Coda now offers OAuth or a hosted MCP server for third-party apps was not confirmed (the MCP docs page was blocked by robots.txt and the Packs OAuth page 404'd).
The exact token-creation menu path is from memory of the docs wording 'My account'.
